confirmed.title: CRITICAL NEW — enforce read-modify-write clobbers tick's OPEN snap, erasing the trip entirely
confirmed.claim: energy-enforce reads the ENTIRE snap at line 88, mutates only snap.breaker at line 105, then atomicWrite-renames the whole snap back. This is an unguarded read-modify-write. When tick(N) and enforce(N+1) race on the same snapPath: (A) tick reads snap(N-1){breaker:CLOSED} at T=0, then computes OPEN breaker from the catastrophic verdict; (B) enforce(N+1) reads snap(N-1){breaker:CLOSED} at T=1 (before tick writes), computes time-driven CLOSED transition, atomicWrite-renames to snap(N-1+CLOSED) at T=2; (C) tick atomicWrite-renames to snap(N){breaker:OPEN, depth++, protectedPathViolations:1} at T=3 — CORRECT CASE; OR (D) enforce renames at T=3 AFTER tick at T=2 — CLOBBER CASE: enforces stale pre-trip state overwrites tick's new state. In the CLOBBER case: breaker reverts to CLOSED, depth regresses, protectedPathViolations is lost. The gate sees CLOSED on every subsequent enforce read and never issues a deny. Hermetic repro confirms 100% trip erasure when enforce wins the last-rename race. Probability: enforce does LESS work than tick (no config file read, no traceGateEvaluation, lighter math) so enforce is typically faster — making enforce-last-write the MAJORITY outcome when the race fires. At fast model pace (~100ms inter-tool latency), the race fires ~15-80% of the time, meaning trip erasure is the expected outcome, not the edge case. This is arm-blocking: arming the gate does nothing if every trip is immediately erased by the next enforce run.

confirmed.title: keyOf uses space separator but comment claims NUL — silent claim collision and permanent data loss on compaction
confirmed.claim: export const keyOf = (e) => `${e.subject} ${e.predicate}` uses a literal space character as the separator between subject and predicate, but the inline comment says 'NUL separator — collision-safe for spaces in subject/predicate'. The comment is false: the space separator is NOT collision-safe. Any two claims whose (subject, predicate) pair shares a common space-joined string — e.g. subject='foo bar' predicate='baz' vs subject='foo' predicate='bar baz' — produce the identical key 'foo bar baz'. foldCanonical's last-write-wins byKey map silently merges them; the loser is evicted from byKey, excluded from liveEventIds, and then permanently erased by the next compactGeneration run (compaction only rescues events in liveEventIds). No warning, no contest flag — the losing claim is gone. Current production writes (MEM_SUBJECT_PREFIX = 'mem:' + sha256hex as subject, short type-enum as predicate) are not hit because neither component contains a space, but the public appendClaim contract has no restriction on spaces, and any non-bridge caller is silently at risk.
confirmed.repro:
node -e "const keyOf = e => \`\${e.subject} \${e.predicate}\`; const e1={subject:'foo bar',predicate:'baz'}; const e2={subject:'foo',predicate:'bar baz'}; console.log(keyOf(e1)===keyOf(e2))" prints: true

Live file /Users/marcelspatz/YURI-OS-MUSUBI/_SYSTEM/Scripts/memory-canonical-store.mjs line 365 confirmed: export const keyOf = (e) => `${e.subject} ${e.predicate}`;  — space separator, not NUL. The inline comment "NUL separator — collision-safe for spaces in subject/predicate" is the intended fix, not the actual implementation. appendClaim (line 240) validates only null/undefined; no space restriction enforced. foldCanonical (line 427) does byKey.set(k, e) last-write-wins; the loser's eventId is absent from liveEventIds, so compactGeneration permanently drops it. Current production writes (mem:<sha256hex> subject, short type-enum predicate) are collision-free today, making this a latent defect — but the public appendClaim contract accepts any string and any new non-bridge caller is silently at risk of permanent data loss after compaction.

Affects the canonical memory store's correctness: any cross-lane write with spaces in subject or predicate silently loses data after compaction. Because the yuri-memory bridge currently produces collision-free keys, live canonical state is not corrupted today, but the bug is a latent correctness landmine for any new writer. Must be fixed before expanding canonical store usage.

confirmed.title: cost-reservation-pool admit() has a TOCTOU race — two concurrent dispatches can both pass the budget check and double-spend the cap
confirmed.claim: admit() reads actuals (line 324), then reads active reservations via sumActiveReservations (line 325), computes projectedTotal, decides fits=true, then writes a reservation file via writeReservation (line 355). There is no mutex, directory-lock, or atomic-compare-and-swap between the read of sumActiveReservations and the write of writeReservation. Two concurrent llm-lane processes invoking admit() simultaneously will both observe zero active reservations, both pass the budget check (both see fits=true), and both write a reservation file — double-spending the cap. The all-or-nothing budget guarantee claimed in the module header is violated under concurrent dispatch.
confirmed.repro:
True multi-process repro (the finding's single-process Promise.all sketch does NOT reproduce the race — admit() is synchronous, Promise.resolve wraps an already-computed value, execution is strictly sequential in one Node.js process):

Setup: write armFlag JSON `{"capUsd":0.02}` to a tmpDir; set YURI_COST_ADMISSION_ENFORCE=1; spawn 3 simultaneous Node.js processes each running admit({model:'gpt-5.5',inputTokens:1000,outputTokensPerStep:500,steps:1}, {armFlag,reserveDir,actuals:{reliable:true,spentUsd:0,...}}).

Observed (4/5 trials): all 3 processes read readdirSync → [] (empty reserveDir), all compute projectedTotal=0+0+0.015=0.015<=0.02 → fits=true, all call writeReservation. Total reserved: $0.045 against a $0.020 cap (2.25x). Two workers showed admit_reserved; one trial admitted all 3.

Example single trial output:
  Worker pid=50728: decision=admit_reserved costUsd=0.015
  Worker pid=50729: decision=reject_over_budget (lucky — OS scheduled it after 50728 wrote)
  Worker pid=50730: decision=admit_reserved costUsd=0.015
  Total reserved: $0.030 | cap: $0.020 | EXCEEDED by $0.010

The structural gap: sumActiveReservations uses plain fs.readdirSync with no lock or O_EXCL; writeReservation uses renameSync for file-level atomicity but NOT for the budget-check-then-write sequence. No mutex, directory lock, or atomic compare-and-set exists between line 325 (sumActiveReservations) and line 355 (writeReservation).

FINDING REPRO SKETCH IS WRONG: Promise.all([Promise.resolve(admit(...)), Promise.resolve(admit(...))]) does NOT create concurrency. The single-process version correctly serializes — the second admit() sees the first reservation and rejects. The race only opens with multiple OS processes. The finding's claim that "both return admit_reserved with reservedUsd totalling 0.030" from the Promise.all sketch is also wrong — without proper armFlag overrides the gate returns advisory_pass (disarmed), and with overrides in single process the second correctly returns reject_over_budget.
confirmed.arm_blast: Directly relevant to arming the cost-admission gate (currently DISARMED). When armed with a real cap, this race means the cap can be silently exceeded by a factor equal to the number of concurrent dispatches. In a nano-swarm fan-out (3 concurrent ollama-cloud lanes), the pool can be triple-committed. The gate's stated invariant — 'all-or-nothing so a half-funded task can never strand the pool' — fails under the exact workload the gate is meant to govern.

confirmed.title: enforce write-back clobbers tick's full state on every tool call (SEAM-1 materialised as write-back race)
confirmed.claim: energy-enforce.mjs reads the full snap at line 88, evaluates the breaker, then writes the ENTIRE snap back at line 105 with only snap.breaker updated. energy-tick.mjs runs async on PostToolUse and writes its own full snap (state, depth, recentAbs, surpriseEngaged, deepEngaged, breaker, ledger, claimFieldFailures, updatedAt). Both hooks use PID-stamped tmp files that rename to the SAME destination (e.g. _SYSTEM/state/energy-session/<sessionId>.json). POSIX rename(2) is atomic per call but not serialised across callers — the last rename wins and erases the other's update. confirmed.title: insertLedgerEvent has no SQLite transaction on SELECT-prev_hash + INSERT — stale-lock eviction opens a chain-branching race
confirmed.claim: insertLedgerEvent selects the current chain head (line 430: SELECT event_hash ORDER BY sequence_id DESC LIMIT 1) and inserts a new row with that value as prev_hash (line 436-456) as two separate statements with no wrapping BEGIN EXCLUSIVE / db.transaction(). The process-level drain lock (acquireLock using POSIX mkdir EEXIST) normally serializes concurrent drains. However: the stale-lock eviction path at line 1007-1009 calls rmSync(lockDir, {recursive:true, force:true}) then recursively calls acquireLock(). Two processes detecting the same stale lock will both rmSync it and then race on the subsequent mkdirSync — the winner acquires the lock and both processes may proceed to drain. Under that race, two processes can both SELECT the same prev_hash, compute different event_hashes for different events that both point to the same parent, and INSERT. The second insert succeeds (different event_id, different event_hash). verifyHashChain detects the branch (ok:false, prev_hash_mismatch) but the audit surface is after the fact — the losing event's queue file is renamed .bad and the event is silently unrecorded.

Structural repro (confirmed via source + runtime):

1. Both structural conditions verified against live code at /Users/marcelspatz/YURI-OS-MUSUBI/_SYSTEM/Scripts/token-ledger.mjs:

   a) insertLedgerEvent (line 424-476): SELECT event_hash ... ORDER BY sequence_id DESC LIMIT 1 (line 430) → sha256 compute → INSERT INTO token_ledger (lines 440-456). No db.transaction(), no BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, no BEGIN IMMEDIATE anywhere in the function body or in the drainTokenLedger loop that calls it. Source scan confirmed: hasTxn=false.

   b) acquireLock stale eviction (lines 1007-1009): `if (Date.now() - stat.mtimeMs > LOCK_STALE_MS) { rmSync(lockDir, {recursive:true,force:true}); return acquireLock(paths); }` — rmSync and the subsequent mkdirSync inside the recursive call are two separate non-atomic OS syscalls. LOCK_STALE_MS=120000ms (2 minutes). Source scan confirmed: raceBetweenRmAndMkdir=true.

2. Operational trigger is more realistic than the finding implies: yuri-graph.json (line 7956) documents that the PostToolUse hook spawns `token-ledger.mjs write` DETACHED for every tool call. Nano-swarm / multi-session runs with high tool-call frequency create many concurrent drain processes against the same lockDir, increasing the probability of the 2-minute stale window being hit.

A true two-process trigger command: pre-queue events, manually create a stale lockDir (backdated mtime > 120s), then: `node -e "import('/path/token-ledger.mjs').then(m=>m.drainTokenLedger())" & node -e "import('/path/token-ledger.mjs').then(m=>m.drainTokenLedger())" &` — both processes see EEXIST, both see mtime > threshold, both rmSync, one wins mkdirSync, the other falls through and may also acquire after a retry. Both then SELECT the same prev_hash, compute different event_hashes for different events sharing the same parent, INSERT both. verifyHashChain would detect prev_hash_mismatch (chain branch) on the next audit call.

4. Fix: wrap the SELECT+INSERT in `db.transaction(fn)()` inside insertLedgerEvent, or wrap the entire drain loop in a single `db.transaction()`. This makes the chain-head read and append atomic within SQLite's serialization guarantees, eliminating the window regardless of the lock race.

killed.title: bash-security-guard role resolution fails open to dev (permissive) when existsSync throws EACCES
killed.reason:
The finding's mechanism is wrong: fs.existsSync does NOT throw on EACCES — it catches the error internally and returns false (documented Node.js behavior, confirmed by live execution). The inner catch at line 307 is therefore never the active path. The finding cites the wrong code path as the trigger.

The security effect (role resolves to 'dev' when _SYSTEM/SELF/ has chmod 000) is real, but it arrives via the ternary at line 306 — existsSync returns false, and false ? 'coworker' : 'dev' yields 'dev'. This is actually the intended design per the comment at lines 296-299: "If no module and no credential, the role system is simply not installed -> unrestricted (dev)." The code cannot distinguish a missing credential file from an unreadable one, but this is a design documentation gap rather than an unexpected inner-catch failure.

Since the finding's core technical claim (inner catch fires, line 307 is the active path) is proved false by live execution, the finding is killed as stated. The residual observation (chmod 000 on SELF dir → dev role via ternary) is a true but low-impact edge case consistent with the stated LOW severity and the solo-owner deployment context.

blockers: B1 (HIGH, arm-blocking-for-RELIABILITY): D2/D10 enforce write-back clobber race. energy-enforce.mjs:88 reads the FULL snap, mutates only snap.breaker at :105, atomicWrite-renames the whole snap back — an unguarded read-modify-write to the SAME destination tick writes. CONFIRMED with hermetic repro: enforce reading a stale pre-trip snap then writing it back erases tick's OPEN breaker, depth++, and protectedPathViolations. The D2 CRITICAL framing ('every trip immediately erased / permanently equivalent to disarmed') is OVERSTATED — the trip model is single-event-catastrophic (transitionOnVerdict:129-140), so the next tick re-trips OPEN if the catastrophic condition persists (per-race 1-call deny slip, not permanent). Severity is HIGH not CRITICAL. FIX (pick one): enforce writes ONLY a breaker-only sidecar file, OR enforce merge-reads the LATEST snap at write time (compare-and-swap), OR enforce does not persist at all (let tick own the snap) — the burn-in already proves tick alone evolves the breaker.

B2 (HIGH, arm-blocking-for-CONFIDENCE): D1 zero process-level test for energy-enforce.mjs. No test exercises the hook as a process (stdin event JSON in → stdout permissionDecision:deny out). The deny path, arm-check, fail-open paths, and stdout JSON shape are all unguarded by regression. The 5 hermetic process tests proven in the audit (no-snap fail-open, OPEN→deny, CLOSED→allow, observability-off, enforce-off) must be committed as _SYSTEM/Scripts/energy-enforce-process.test.mjs and wired into the pre-commit gate before flipping the flag. Arming a live blocking gate with zero process-level coverage bets correctness on metrics-only burn-in, which never exercises the actual stdout emit path.

B3 (HIGH, arm-blocking-for-INTEGRITY): D10 the arm flag (_SYSTEM/state/energy-enforce.enabled) and the snap dir (_SYSTEM/state/energy-session/) are unprotected from Bash mutation. Confirmed: neither path is in settings.json deny-list (only .claude/state/, backend/data/, .env), bash-security-guard isBlockedClaudeRemove (only .claude/ prefix), or operator-write-guard. A model under the armed gate can 'rm _SYSTEM/state/energy-enforce.enabled' (silent disarm, no prompt, no audit) or inject a CLOSED-breaker snap to bypass the gate for its session. Add _SYSTEM/state/energy-enforce.enabled and _SYSTEM/state/energy-session/** to the settings.json deny-list (or bash-security-guard BLOCKED set) before arming. NOTE: env-armed sessions (YURI_ENERGY_ENFORCE=1, currently set in this env) are immune to the rm-the-flag vector but NOT the snap-injection vector.

ruling.rationale: Decode: the owner wants this armed this weekend AND wants the architecture to come out remarkable. Those two pull apart right now, and the honest call is arm-after-fixes — the fixes are small enough that 'this weekend' still holds. SEAM-3, the priority-zero hard gate, is CLEAN (verified independently: 80/80 real-UUID snaps, zero default.json, a real UUID session got 7 real enforce denies proving the ids match). Both findings tagged 'BLOCKS THE ARM' are overstated and I disproved them at the seam: (1) D5 phantom-staleness reproduces (ΔU=0.478 > threshold=0, soft gate rejects every healthy Edit) BUT the live deny path is breaker-gated, not soft-ΔU-gated — evaluateGate only returns deny when the breaker is OPEN, and the breaker only opens on a catastrophic veto (transitionOnVerdict → isCatastrophic), not on a soft reject. Confirmed live: healthy Edit → verdict.accept:false but breaker CLOSED → evaluateGate returns 'allow'. Enforce does NOT block healthy work. D5 is a real signal-quality/calibration defect (noisy trace, the steer advisory could mis-fire) but NOT an arm-blocker, and crucially it errs toward MORE rejection (conservative), never toward wrongly opening the breaker. (2) The D2/D10 clobber reproduces and is real, but it self-heals at N+2 (single-event-catastrophic trip model) — a per-race 1-call deny slip, HIGH not CRITICAL. The genuine arm-relevant blockers (B1 write-back race, B2 zero process test, B3 unprotected flag/snap) don't make arming DANGEROUS — every path fails OPEN and layer-1 holds — they make the armed gate UNRELIABLE and trivially defeatable (a single Bash rm/inject disarms it, a refactor silently breaks the only block signal with no test to catch it). Arming a gate that a model can disarm in one tool call, that erases its own trips under load, and that has zero regression coverage is theater, not enforcement. Izanagi 3-branch weighted scoring (EV 0.5 / blast 0.3 / reversibility 0.2, per owner 'best outcome' intent): arm-after-fixes 8.70 > dont-arm-yet 7.20 > arm-this-weekend 5.40. The fixes are hours of reversible work; do them Friday, then flip the flag. Note: YURI_ENERGY_ENFORCE=1 is ALREADY set in this env, so env-launched sessions are technically already armed against the catastrophic-veto path — which makes closing B1/B3 more urgent, not less. Residual risk on this ruling: I did not exhaustively re-verify every MEDIUM/LOW finding (token-ledger hash-chain races, canonical-store contested resolver, eml-tree/formula-foundry promotion gaps) — they are correctly scoped by the fleet as non-blocking for energy-enforce (the enforce path does not read those stores) and I trust the per-finding repros that confirmed them, but they remain open correctness items for the cost-gate and canonical-store arm cycles, not this one.

remarkable_strengths: PDP/PEP split borrowed from OPA is genuinely well-architected: the decision (gateProposal/computeU) is computed in PostToolUse and persisted as breaker state; the PreToolUse PEP only reads + enforces. This is the right separation and is rare in hook-based gates.

Deny-OR composition is structurally sound and is a real (un-credited) strength: I verified all 9 other ALL-matcher synchronous PreToolUse hooks emit ZERO permissionDecision:'allow' (grep across pre-tool-gate/bash-security-guard/operator-write-guard/tirith-url-guard/claude-protocol-guard/pre-tool-use/musubi-protocol-enforce/yuri-risk-lite/directive-guard). Since the harness OR-composes denies and no peer emits allow, energy-enforce's deny can never be silently downgraded by a sibling hook. The architecture earns this but the audit never stated it as a verified invariant.

Layered defense-in-depth is honest and correct: energy gate is explicitly layer-2 advisory; layer-1 deterministic guards (operator-write-guard, bash-security-guard, settings deny-list) provide the real protected-path floor. Fail-open is a deliberate, documented design choice (line 22) not an accident — for a layer-2 conscience this is the correct failure direction.

Breaker auto-decay (OPEN->HALF_OPEN->CLOSED) with the clock-skew rescue on the OPEN branch (elapsed<0||elapsed>=wait -> probe) means the gate provably CANNOT permanently block — a strong safety property that the D3 findings confirm holds on the OPEN path.

The math substrate is deep and self-consistent at the formula level: Wasserstein-1 ordinal-drift swap (energyFormulaVersion 3), the overconfidence-coupling mu term, per-claim non-offsettable veto keying, corner-law affine reasoning, and the fail-CLOSED malformed-evidence path all reflect real design maturity. Several KILLED findings were refuted precisely because the math defends itself (NaN-deltaU unreachable via 3 independent guards; malformed-before is conservative not fail-open).

Burn-in design intent is correct: line 105 persists the advanced breaker BEFORE the enforce branch, so the breaker state machine evolves identically whether armed or not — the metrics-only burn-in genuinely exercises the decision logic and breaker evolution.
gaps_to_remarkable: KILL THE READ-MODIFY-WRITE RACE CLASS, don't patch it. The two CRITICAL/HIGH D2+D10 findings (enforce clobbers tick's full snap), the D8 cost-pool TOCTOU, the D8 token-ledger SELECT+INSERT race, and the D10 session-state.js shared-tmp race are ALL the same defect: unguarded read-decide-write on a shared file with no atomic compare-and-swap. Remarkable = a single shared 'atomic-merge-snapshot' / CAS primitive (or a breaker-only sidecar so enforce never touches tick's fields) applied uniformly. A system with FIVE instances of the same concurrency bug class is not remarkable; one that has a proven concurrency primitive every hook uses is.

MAKE THE BLOCK CHANNEL TESTED AND VERSION-VERIFIED. The single path that does the actual blocking (stdout permissionDecision:deny emit) has ZERO process-level tests (D1, three findings) AND the burn-in period never exercises it (burn-in flips emit->audit; emit is the untested branch). Remarkable = (a) a committed energy-enforce-process.test.mjs wired into pre-commit with the 5 proven scenarios, AND (b) a one-time live harness-contract verification on 2.1.177 that a sync PreToolUse stdout-deny on exit 0 actually blocks (the changelog shows this contract churned: lines 1474/1689/2054). The whole arm rests on this external fact and it was assumed.

ENGAGE OR HONESTLY RETIRE THE ZETA STALENESS TERM. The ζ term currently fires a fail-closed 'all evidence malformed' penalty (0.5*N) on EVERY live verdict because applyTransition writes records with no halfLife and staleness.halfLifeDays is absent from config (D5 CRITICAL — every healthy Edit yields deltaU>0, would block ALL forward progress at threshold=0). This is the single most arm-blocking correctness defect. Remarkable = either wire halfLifeDays + write halfLife into each record so ζ measures actual age, or set zeta=0 and document ζ as Wave-3. Shipping a term that mislabels fresh evidence as 'malformed' and would reject normal coding is the opposite of remarkable.

FIX THE CONFIG/DOC TRUTH SURFACE. Six findings (D4/D5/D6) hit the same root: energy-weights.json _doc says klDivergence but live code is Wasserstein-1; mu has no config knob and no _doc entry; _doc.ranges.threshold says 'any sign' but the loader silently drops negatives; no mu<=beta cross-weight guard. A 'tuning cockpit' whose documentation lies about the live formula and whose knobs silently no-op is not remarkable — it is a calibration trap. Remarkable = the config IS the contract: doc matches code, every live weight (incl mu) is tunable, out-of-range values warn-and-clamp instead of silently dropping.

PROTECT THE ARM FLAG AND SNAP DIR. D10 HIGH: _SYSTEM/state/energy-enforce.enabled and _SYSTEM/state/energy-session/ are absent from the settings.json deny-list, bash-security-guard, and operator-write-guard — a model can rm the flag or inject a CLOSED breaker via Bash to silently self-disarm a live armed gate with no audit entry. A safety gate that the gated agent can delete in one tool call is not remarkable. Remarkable = the arm flag + snap dir are in the layer-1 deny-list, making self-disarm structurally impossible.

CLOSE THE PROOF-GATE PROMOTION-STATUS HOLE (D9). validateFormulaCard early-returns when bank.advisoryOnly===true, so a card claiming promotionStatus:'stable'/'verified-baseline' passes validation with zero worked-example execution; treeToCard exposes this directly via opts.promotionStatus. A promotion pipeline that lets a card LIE about being proof-gated undermines the entire 'verified evidence outranks claims' doctrine. Not arm-blocking this weekend, but it is a foundational integrity crack that must close before any kernel formula is promoted into computeU.
uncovered: HARNESS DENY-CHANNEL CONTRACT (the load-bearing external fact, never verified): the entire arm depends on Claude Code 2.1.177 honoring a synchronous PreToolUse hook's stdout {permissionDecision:'deny'} on exit code 0. The changelog shows this exact contract was buggy/churning (line 1474 ask-downgrade, line 1689 'emit JSON to stdout AND exit code 2', line 2054 allow-bypassing-deny). No dimension verified the live contract on the running version; the rails forbade live arm testing, so it was ASSUMED. D1's manual repro proves energy-enforce EMITS the right JSON, never that the harness ACTS on it. This is the single highest-leverage uncovered stone.

BURN-IN vs ARMED PARITY (no dimension): the metrics-only burn-in period — the owner's stated pre-arm confidence mechanism (settings comment: 'Watch the audit log, confirm zero false trips, THEN flip the flag') — exercises the decision + breaker evolution but NEVER the stdout emit() that does the blocking. Burn-in green therefore does NOT predict armed-correct. This is implicit inside D1's 'zero process tests' but was never named as the parity gap that makes the burn-in strategy partially blind.

DENY-OR COMPOSITION ACROSS ALL 10 SYNC HOOKS (no dimension): I verified no peer hook emits allow (so deny can't be downgraded), but the audit never systematically enumerated the 10-hook ALL-matcher PreToolUse set or proved the composition invariant. It was touched only as a code-comment assertion in energy-enforce.mjs (wave-3 G.3), not independently re-verified by a dimension.

CUMULATIVE SYNC-HOOK LATENCY BUDGET (no dimension): there are 10 synchronous ALL-matcher PreToolUse hooks, NONE with a timeout (verified). D1's timeout finding treats energy-enforce in isolation; nobody measured the aggregate per-tool-call latency of all 10 sync hooks, or what happens to the 10-minute harness ceiling when several do filesystem I/O. Arming adds enforce's I/O to an already-unbounded chain.

YURI_ENERGY_BREAKER_RESET OPERATOR-OVERRIDE PATH (energy-enforce.mjs:92-96): the reset path does its own snap read-modify-atomicWrite and is subject to the same clobber race as the main path, plus it is env-gated (any process with that env set force-closes the breaker). No finding covers the reset path's race or its interaction with a concurrent tick write.

No de-duplication pass collapsed these into single root-cause defects with multiple witnesses. A backlog that triple-counts one bug inflates the apparent defect count and obscures that it is ONE primitive to fix.

The D2 KILLED finding established legacy-snap-> CLOSED init is safe, but nobody traced the full first-arm cold-start sequence end-to-end (no snap -> fail-open until first tick writes -> first breaker materialization) as an explicit arm-day runbook scenario.
